## Context / Problem

Epic 62dc's criteria 2, 3 and 4 are undelivered: `rebar create` does not surface semantically similar existing tickets, so agents re-file work that already has a ticket. ADR 0122 (`docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md`, Accepted 2026-10-31) measured the retrieval candidates and is the binding evidence. This ticket is the container for building what it specifies; its children carry the work.

The create-time advisory that exists today is a same-title journal only: `duplicate_create_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:117-119`), gated by `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (`:129`), matching on `title_norm` equality (`:103`). ADR 0122 measured that stratum at 1,431 of 1,524 recorded duplicate pairs; the 93 differing-title pairs are what this work exists to catch.

**ADR 0122 decided retrieval quality, not portability.** It compared four candidates on this store and adopted `vector` — a Titan v2 embedding of a Haiku digest — reaching semantic recall@5 0.876 against the `fts5` baseline's 0.823 (p=0.0213, the only distinguishable win over the free baseline at k=5). It did not consider that rebar ships to environments with diverse model providers, or none. A retrieval path reachable only through one vendor's embedding endpoint would make the feature unavailable to most installations, which the blocking `project.portability` criterion forbids.

## Approach

Build retrieval in two tiers, with the portable one as the default and the measured one as an opt-in upgrade. The epic already requires a lexical fallback as a degradation path; making it the default rather than only the failure mode is what makes the feature portable, and ADR 0122's own numbers show the cost is small and bounded.

- **Lexical tier, the default.** sqlite FTS5 with bm25 weights title 5.0 / description 1.0, the configuration ADR 0122 measured as its `fts5` baseline (`evals/similar-tickets/measure.py:389-396`). It needs no credentials, no network and no provider, so it works in every installation. Semantic recall@5 0.823 against `vector`'s 0.876, and distinguishably better than `vector` at lexical recall@10 (0.993 vs 0.972, p=0.0000) — ADR 0122's stated reason for not removing it.
- **Embedding tier, opt-in.** The digest-and-embed path ADR 0122 adopted, reached through a configured embedding model rather than a hardcoded vendor call.

**Portability is delivered by the lexical tier, not by the embedding tier.** pydantic-ai 1.107.9 — already the runtime behind `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` — exposes a first-class embeddings API (`Embedder`, `EmbeddingModel`, `infer_embedding_model`, `KnownEmbeddingModelName`) with backends for `bedrock`, `openai`, `cohere`, `google`, `voyageai` and `sentence_transformers`, plus `OpenAIEmbeddingsCompatibleProvider` for arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoints. That makes the embedding tier provider-agnostic, which is necessary but not sufficient for portability: every one of those backends still requires either credentials or a model download. `sentence_transformers` is not installed in this environment, needs the optional `pydantic-ai-slim[sentence-transformers]` group, and fetches weights from HuggingFace on first use, so it is not a zero-dependency offline path and is not relied on as one. `TestEmbeddingModel` is a test double and is not portability evidence either.

So the feature is available everywhere because its default tier needs no model at all. Dispatching the opt-in tier on a `provider:model` string is the same shape rebar already uses for chat models, making it a config key over an existing mechanism rather than a new provider abstraction.

`bedrock:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` is the configured default because it is what ADR 0122 measured. An installation that cannot reach it configures another model or runs lexical-only; in neither case does the feature become unavailable.

Surfacing reuses the advisory-field seam `duplicate_warning` already proves end to end, rather than adding a second create-time notification path. That seam carries an optional advisory on the create result for the library and MCP as a result key (`src/rebar/types.py:276`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:179`), and on CLI stderr so stdout stays pure (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:467`); it is already described in `src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json`.

The seam spans **four** create surfaces, not three: `rebar idea` is a distinct path that re-emits advisories itself (`src/rebar/_commands/idea.py:92-93`) from its own return dict (`_lib_writes.py:224,:231`). Because every site names its advisory keys individually, a key added only to `create` is silently dropped from `idea`. The surfacing child therefore makes advisory pass-through generic rather than hand-copying one more key.

Sequencing follows the walking skeleton. The lexical tier delivers the whole user-visible feature with no provider dependency, so the index and surfacing design is proven end to end before any paid call is wired in. The embedding tier then swaps the ranking function behind an interface that already has a working implementation and a measured baseline to beat.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar create` returns at most 5 similar existing tickets as an advisory field carrying id, alias, title and score. Checked by: the surfacing child's shape tests.
- [x] That advisory is present on CLI `--output json`, the library `create_ticket` return dict, MCP `create_ticket`, and `rebar idea`. Checked by: one parity test per surface.
- [x] Warm-index retrieval holds a p95 below the cold-catch-up p95 divided by the recorded warm-to-cold ratio, on a synthetic store of at least 10,000 tickets, recomputing zero hashes. Checked by: a timing test asserting store size and hash count before measuring. Relative, not an absolute 500 ms: ADR 0122 records that bar at 107 ms locally but 545 ms on `macos-latest`.
- [x] The cold-catch-up p95 is measured and recorded in ADR 0122. Checked by: the ADR containing the figure.
- [x] After 100 creates and 100 reads against a test store, the `tickets` branch contains only user event types. Checked by: an integration test asserting the branch's event-type set.
- [x] A ticket created on a clone is findable by the next create on that same clone, in one process, with no daemon, background thread, MCP server or CI involved. Checked by: an integration test.
- [x] With no model provider configured and no network reachable, retrieval returns ranked results on the lexical tier. Checked by: an integration test clearing every provider credential environment variable.
- [x] A create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory when the index is absent, when catch-up fails, when the configured embedding provider denies or errors, and when the digest parse yields empty fields. Checked by: one test per failure mode asserting the create's exit status and advisory contents.
- [x] Each of those failure modes emits a diagnostic. Checked by: the same tests capturing logs.

## Child decomposition

- **Lexical index and catch-up** — the FTS5 index, the persisted ticket-dir to dir-hash map, enumeration-based catch-up, ranking, and the degradation paths. The walking skeleton: the whole retrieval capability for an installation with no model provider.
- **Surfacing across create and idea** — generic advisory pass-through and the advisory field on all four create surfaces, plus the schema contract.
- **ADR 0122 amendments** — the two-tier decision, the deployment precondition narrowed to the embedding tier, and the measured cold-catch-up p95.
- **Embedding tier over the pydantic-ai embeddings seam** — the digest step, the configured embedding model, vector ranking, and the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer.
- **Bedrock IAM widening for the Titan embedding model** — admits the configured default embedding model in this deployment. It gates that default here; it does not gate the feature, which ships working on the lexical tier regardless.
